dorset-culture.name: Dorset culture
dorset-culture.summary: A Paleo-Eskimo culture in the North American Arctic, lasting from about 500 BCE until it died out by 1000–1500 CE, before the Thule (proto-Inuit) arrived. Inuit legends recall its people as the Tuniit.

medieval-warm-period.name: Medieval Warm Period
medieval-warm-period.summary: A period of warm climate in the North Atlantic region lasting from about 950 to 1250 CE, not uniform worldwide and followed by the cooler Little Ice Age.

erik-the-red.name: Erik the Red
erik-the-red.summary: Norse explorer (c. 950–c. 1003) credited with founding the first European settlement in Greenland after being exiled from Iceland around 982.

gunnbj-rn-ulfsson.name: Gunnbjörn Ulfsson
gunnbj-rn-ulfsson.summary: A Norse explorer from Norway and later Iceland, credited as the first European to sight Greenland after being blown off course; Greenland's highest mountain is named after him.

western-settlement.name: Western Settlement
western-settlement.summary: A Norse farming community in medieval Greenland founded around 985, smaller than its companion Eastern Settlement and found abandoned when last visited in the 14th century.

qulliq.name: Qulliq
qulliq.summary: A traditional oil lamp used by circumpolar peoples including the Inuit, fueled by seal oil or blubber and made of soapstone; a vital source of Arctic warmth and light.

ipiutak-site.name: Ipiutak site
ipiutak-site.summary: A large archaeological site at Point Hope, Alaska, with over 500 house remains and rich ivory carvings, representing the Ipiutak culture that existed from about 100 BCE to 800 CE.

point-hope-alaska.name: Point Hope, Alaska
point-hope-alaska.summary: A remote city on Alaska's northwestern coast with no road connections, and site of the ancient Ipiutak culture known for elaborate ivory carvings.

birnirk-culture.name: Birnirk culture
birnirk-culture.summary: A prehistoric Inuit archaeological culture that flourished from the 6th to 12th centuries along Alaska's North Slope and Russia's Chukchi Peninsula, known for advanced harpoon technology.

chukchi-peninsula.name: Chukchi Peninsula
chukchi-peninsula.summary: The easternmost point of continental Asia, located at about 66° N, 172° W.

deering-alaska.name: Deering
deering-alaska.summary: A small city in Alaska's Northwest Arctic Borough, located where the Inmachuk River meets Kotzebue Sound, with a 2020 population of 182.

saga-of-the-greenlanders.name: Saga of the Greenlanders
saga-of-the-greenlanders.summary: One of two main Icelandic sources on the Norse colonization of North America, describing events around 1000 CE, including six expeditions from Greenland led by figures such as Leif Erikson and Freydís Eiríksdóttir.

saga-of-erik-the-red.name: Saga of Erik the Red
saga-of-erik-the-red.summary: A 13th-century Icelandic saga on Norse exploration of North America, mainly chronicling the expedition of Thorfinn Karlsefni and Gudrid, including Erik the Red's exile to Greenland and Leif Erikson's discovery of Vinland.

markland.name: Markland
markland.summary: One of three lands on North America's Atlantic coast, south of Helluland and north of Vinland, discovered by Leif Eriksson around 1000 AD; likely visited later for timber though never settled.

helluland.name: Helluland
helluland.summary: One of three lands sighted by Bjarni Herjólfsson and explored by Norse voyagers around 1000 CE on the North Atlantic coast of North America, alongside Vinland and Markland.

vinland.name: Vinland
vinland.summary: Area of coastal North America explored by Vikings, where Leif Erikson landed around AD 1000, long before Columbus; Norse building remains confirming it were found at L'Anse aux Meadows, Newfoundland, in 1960.

vinland-sagas.name: Vinland sagas
vinland-sagas.summary: Two Icelandic texts, the Saga of the Greenlanders and the Saga of Erik the Red, written in the early 13th century about events from around 970 to 1030; the main source on Norse voyages to Vinland.

leif-erikson.name: Leif Erikson
leif-erikson.summary: A Norse explorer (c. 970s–c. 1018/1025) thought to be the first European to reach continental America, establishing a settlement at Vinland about five centuries before Columbus.

procopius.name: Procopius
procopius.summary: A Greek historian from Caesarea, about 500 to 565, who accompanied the Byzantine general Belisarius and became the principal historian of Emperor Justinian's era.

pytheas.name: Pytheas
pytheas.summary: Greek geographer and explorer from Massalia (born c. 350 BC) who sailed to Northern Europe around 325 BC, circumnavigating Britain and becoming the first to describe the Arctic and the midnight sun.

tunulliarfik-fjord.name: Tunulliarfik Fjord
tunulliarfik-fjord.summary: A fjord in southern Greenland known in Norse times as Eiriksfjord, where Erik the Red settled after being banished from Iceland.

l-anse-aux-meadows.name: L'Anse aux Meadows
l-anse-aux-meadows.summary: A Norse settlement site on Newfoundland's northern tip, dated to around 1000 CE by carbon and tree-ring evidence, the only confirmed pre-Columbian European site in the Americas outside Greenland.

helge-ingstad.name: Helge Ingstad
helge-ingstad.summary: A Norwegian explorer (1899–2001) who, with his wife Anne Stine Ingstad, discovered a Viking settlement at L'Anse aux Meadows in Newfoundland in 1960, proving Norse crossings to North America centuries before Columbus.

anne-stine-ingstad.name: Anne Stine Ingstad
anne-stine-ingstad.summary: Norwegian archaeologist who, with her husband Helge Ingstad, discovered the remains of a Norse settlement at L'Anse aux Meadows in 1960, proving Norse voyages to North America centuries before Columbus.

kayak.name: Kayak
kayak.summary: Small, narrow human-powered boat usually moved with a double-bladed paddle. The traditional kind has an enclosed deck with a cockpit for the paddler.

arctic-small-tool-tradition.name: Arctic Small Tool tradition
arctic-small-tool-tradition.summary: A prehistoric culture that arose around Alaska and the Bering Strait about 2500 BC, marked by a microblade toolkit, whose people were the first to settle Arctic Canada and Greenland.

saqqaq-culture.name: Saqqaq culture
saqqaq-culture.summary: A Paleo-Inuit culture in southern Greenland, named after the settlement of Saqqaq, and the longest-residing culture in Greenland's history.

pre-dorset.name: Pre-Dorset
pre-dorset.summary: A Paleo-Eskimo culture, or group of cultures, in the Eastern Canadian Arctic from about 3200 to 850 BCE that preceded the Dorset culture.

thule-people.name: Thule people
thule-people.summary: The precursors of modern Inuit and Yupik peoples, who developed in coastal Alaska by 1000 CE, spread across the Arctic, and replaced the earlier Dorset culture by the 15th century.

therkel-mathiassen.name: Therkel Mathiassen
therkel-mathiassen.summary: A Danish archaeologist, anthropologist, and ethnographer (1892–1967) known for his scientific study of the Arctic.

baffin-island.name: Baffin Island
baffin-island.summary: The largest island in Canada and second-largest in the Americas, in Nunavut at 68°N; inhabited for at least 3,000 years, it now has about 13,000 residents.

tuilik.name: Tuilik
tuilik.summary: Inuit watertight jacket worn when paddling a kayak, sealed at the face, wrists and cockpit rim. It lets a paddler roll upright without getting wet, and the trapped air helps with buoyancy.

kayak-roll.name: Kayak roll
kayak-roll.summary: Technique for righting a capsized kayak using body motion and a paddle, without leaving the boat. It is important on serious whitewater, where swimming leaves a paddler more exposed.

norse-settlements-in-greenland.name: Grænlendingar
norse-settlements-in-greenland.summary: Name for the Norse settlers who came to Greenland from Iceland after 986 CE, the first Europeans to explore and briefly settle North America. Their settlements lasted about half a millennium before being abandoned for unclear reasons.

eastern-settlement.name: Eastern Settlement
eastern-settlement.summary: The larger of two main Norse colonies in Greenland, settled around 985 to 1000 CE from Iceland and home to about 4,000 people at its peak, with its last written record dated 1408.

qaqortoq.name: Qaqortoq
qaqortoq.summary: The capital city of the Kujalleq municipality in southern Greenland, located near the site of the Norse Eastern Settlement founded by Icelandic colonists.

nuuk.name: Nuuk
nuuk.summary: Capital and largest city of Greenland, founded in 1728 by Danish-Norwegian missionary Hans Egede as Godthaab; renamed Nuuk after home rule began in 1979.

bjarni-herj-lfsson.name: Bjarni Herjólfsson
bjarni-herj-lfsson.summary: An Icelandic explorer believed to be the first known European to sight the mainland of the Americas, in 986.

christopher-columbus.name: Christopher Columbus
christopher-columbus.summary: Italian explorer and navigator (1451–1506) whose four Spanish-sponsored voyages opened the way for European exploration and colonization of the Americas.

brattahl.name: Brattahlíð
brattahl.summary: Erik the Red's estate in the Eastern Settlement, the Viking colony he founded in southwestern Greenland in the late 10th century, inhabited by his descendants until the mid-15th century.

narsarsuaq.name: Narsarsuaq
narsarsuaq.summary: A small settlement in southern Greenland whose economy long depended on Narsarsuaq Airport, a former U.S. military base, alongside a tourism trade in wildlife, gemstones and glaciers.

ari-thorgilsson.name: Ari Thorgilsson
ari-thorgilsson.summary: Iceland's most prominent medieval chronicler (1067/68–1148), author of Íslendingabók, which recorded the histories of the families who settled Iceland.

slendingab-k.name: Íslendingabók
slendingab-k.summary: A 12th-century historical work on early Icelandic history, written by the priest Ari Þorgilsson; only one of its two original versions has survived.

skr-ling.name: Skræling
skr-ling.summary: The Old Norse name Norse Greenlanders used for peoples they encountered in North America, including the Thule people and, in Vinland, Indigenous inhabitants.

kalaallit.name: Kalaallit
kalaallit.summary: The largest indigenous group in Greenland, part of the Inuit people, whose language, Kalaallisut, is known in English as Greenlandic.

kinngait.name: Kinngait
kinngait.summary: An Inuit hamlet on Dorset Island near Baffin Island in Nunavut, Canada, known as Cape Dorset until 2020.

nunavut.name: Nunavut
nunavut.summary: Canada's largest and northernmost territory, created in 1999 from the Northwest Territories to provide the Inuit with self-government.

herj-lfr-b-r-arson.name: Herjólfr Bárðarson
herj-lfr-b-r-arson.summary: Icelandic settler and companion of Erik the Red who sailed with him to settle Greenland in 985; father of Bjarni Herjúlfsson.

hebrides.name: Hebrides
hebrides.summary: The largest archipelago in Scotland and the British Isles, occupied since the Mesolithic period and shaped by Celtic, Norse and English cultures.

greenlandic-norse.name: Greenlandic Norse
greenlandic-norse.summary: An extinct North Germanic language spoken in Norse Greenland until the settlements' demise in the late 15th century, known mainly from runic inscriptions and believed to have been in contact with the Greenlandic language.
